C14-2026-0019 - Dalton Airport Overlay Rezoning - Conduct a public hearing and approve an ordinance amending City Code Title 25 by zoning property locally known as 1019 Dalton Lane (Carson Creek Watershed). Applicant Request: To zone from interim-rural residence (I-RR) combining district zoning to limited industrial service (LI) district zoning. Staff Recommendation and Zoning and Platting Recommendation: To grant limited industrial service-conditional overlay (LI-CO) combining district zoning. Owner/Applicant: HPI Acquisition, LLC. Agent: Winstead PC (Micah King). City Staff: Cynthia Hadri, Austin Planning, 512-974-7620

Approve a resolution authorizing the filing of eminent domain proceedings and payment to acquire the property interests needed in support of Austin Watershed Protection’s Barton Creek - Oak Acres Creek Flood Risk Reduction Project, for the public use of flood mitigation and to improve roadway access to the neighborhood during large storm events requiring the acquisition of a public utility easement consisting of .0498 of one acre (1,308 square foot) and a temporary working space easement consisting of 0.0300 of one acre (1,308 square foot), both being out of the Thomas Anderson Survey No. 17, Abstract No. 2, Travis County, Texas, being a portion of Lot 24-B, resubdivision of a portion of Oak Acres, a subdivision of record in Book 9, Page 91, Plat Records, Travis County, Texas, said Lot 24-B conveyed to Luis Gonzalez and Maria Calleja by Warranty Deed with Vendor’s Lien dated February 14, 2025, as recorded in Document Number 2025016716, Official Public Records, Travis County, Texas, currently collectively appraised at $7,992, subject to an increase in value based on updated appraisals, a Special Commissioner’s award, negotiated settlement, or judgment. The owners of the needed property are Luis Gonzalez and Maria Calleja. The property is located at 5673 Oak Boulevard, Austin, Texas 78735. The general route of the project is from 5677 Oak Boulevard to 5600 Oak Boulevard, Austin, Texas 78735. Funding: $7,992 is available in the Capital Budget of Austin Watershed Protection.

Approve a resolution directing the City Manager to provide data on the outcomes of each City social services contract, to provide an understanding of the geographical distribution of those individuals and families being served by the City’s social services contracts and report back to Council.

Approve a resolution directing the City Manager to establish a reporting and tracking process, provide quarterly reports to Council, provide updates regarding legislative efforts, convene a sub-quorum of Council Members to guide legislative objectives, address concerns from community organizations, and establish a community advisory group related to the implementation of the No Wrong Door initiative.

Approve a resolution directing the City Manager to work with the Capital Area Metropolitan Planning Organization, the Texas Department of Transportation, and other partners to prioritize safety, walking, biking, and transit in proposed Parmer Lane (Farm to Market Road 734) improvements, and to advocate for a full environmental review of any proposal for the corridor.
Approve an ordinance waiving or reimbursing certain fees related to Sunday Sessions ATX's 2026 Sunday Sessions by Legacy on a Plate held at the Waterloo Park on October 11, 2026.

Approve a resolution directing the City Manager to prepare an ordinance for Council consideration authorizing the City Manager to enter into an agreement that would permit the encroachment into the public right-of-way of Grove Boulevard by a proposed elevated walkway to be constructed, operated, and maintained by Ecology Action of Texas and waiving the application and application fee requirements of City Code Section 14-11-51 (Application and Approval) for the agreement.

Approve an ordinance waiving or reimbursing certain fees related to Austin Sister Cities International's Austin-Taichung 40th Anniversary Celebration held at the Asian American Resource Center on September 19, 2026.

Approve an ordinance amending City Code Chapter 7-2 (Art in Public Places) to add and revise definitions, require City facilities delivered by a public facility corporation to incorporate a two percent allocation of construction cost as defined by Chapter 7-2, encourage private developers to incorporate a two percent allocation of a project’s cost to art, and expand and update language regarding the flexibility of art placement and funding for maintenance, repairs, relocations, and deaccessions. Funding: This item has no fiscal impact. The future financial impact will be determined as specific capital improvement projects and public facility corporation projects are approved.

Authorize negotiation and execution of a Fourth Amendment to the Lease Agreement with Minorities for Equality in Economy, Education, Liberty, and Justice, Inc., a Texas non-profit corporation, on behalf of Austin Public Health, for approximately 738 square feet of City-owned office space located at 403 ½ East 15th Street, Austin, Texas 78701, for a term of five years, with one five-year option to extend, for an annual lease rate of $100.  Funding: This item is projected to result in revenue of $100 in the Operating Budget of Austin Public Health.

Authorize negotiation and execution of all documents and instruments necessary or desirable to acquire, on behalf of Austin Water's Wildlands Conservation as part of the Balcones Canyonlands Preserve (BCP), in fee simple approximately 3.9924 acres and 2.8968 acres (6.8892 acres total) of land generally located south of Ranch Road 2222, west of Oakwood Cove at Beverly Hills Drive in Austin, Travis County, Texas 78731, from Russell G. Coffee a/k/a Russell Graham Coffee and Christine Coffee Baker, as Co-Independent Executors of the Estate of Robert Franklin Coffee, deceased, in Travis County, Texas, Probate Case No. C-1-PB-21-001404 for a total amount not to exceed $3,676,000, including closing costs. Funding: $3,676,000 is available in the Capital Budget of Austin Financial Services.
This item has been removed. Line intentionally left blank.

C14-2026-0026 - Phoenix Motor Works - Conduct a public hearing and approve an ordinance amending City Code Title 25 by rezoning property locally known as 1125 and 1127 West 6th Street (Lady Bird Lake Watershed). Applicant Request: To rezone from general commercial services-mixed use-vertical mixed use building-conditional overlay-neighborhood plan (CS-MU-V-CO-NP) combining district zoning to limited industrial service-planned development area-neighborhood plan (LI-PDA-NP) combining district zoning. Staff Recommendation and Planning Commission Recommendation: To grant limited industrial service-planned development area-neighborhood plan (LI-PDA-NP) combining district zoning. Owner/Applicant: SDC PMW, LLC. Agent: Alice Glasco Consulting (Alice Glasco). City Staff: Cynthia Hadri, Austin Planning, 512-974-7620.

Authorize an amendment to a contract for continued performance and employee engagement software licenses, assessments, and training for all City departments with Gallup, Inc., to extend the term by two years and increase the amount by $1,257,000 for a revised total contract amount not to exceed $1,351,000. Funding: $233,000 is available in the Fiscal Year 2026-2027 Operating Budgets of various City departments. Funding for the remaining contract term is contingent upon available funding in future budgets.
Approve a resolution casting a vote for Na’Cole Thompson as the Region 10 director of the Texas Municipal League.

Authorize a contract for workers’ compensation medical management services to administer the City’s physician panel, manage medical costs, and support employee return to work for Austin Human Resources with Injury Management Organization, for an initial term of two years in an estimated amount of $2,900,000 with up to three one-year extension options each in variable amounts for a total contract amount not to exceed $7,590,000. Funding: $1,450,000 is available in the Workers’ Compensation Fund of Austin Human Resources. Funding for the remaining contract term is contingent upon available funding in future budgets.

Authorize negotiation and execution of an amendment to the Agreement for Wholesale Wastewater Utility Service for the Comanche Canyon Ranch Extraterritorial Jurisdiction Planned Unit Development with Travis County Water Control and Improvement District No. 17 (WCID 17), allowing Austin Water to receive untreated wastewater for treatment, in place of treated wastewater currently provided under the existing agreement. This amendment supports WCID 17’s evaluation of decommissioning its treatment facility and reflects Austin Water’s ability to accommodate the operational change without additional efforts or cost. Funding: This item has no fiscal impact. WCID 17 will assume the costs for decommissioning its Comanche Canyon Ranch Wastewater Treatment Plant.
Approve a resolution affirming Council’s commitment to support workers and directing the City Manager to develop and incentivize a qualified, local workforce in certain Convention Center contracts.

The Mayor will recess the City Council meeting to conduct a Board of Directors’ meeting of the Austin Housing Finance Corporation. Following the adjournment of the AHFC Board meeting, the City Council will reconvene. This item has no fiscal impact.

Conduct a public hearing in accordance with Texas Parks and Wildlife Code Chapter 26 and consider a resolution authorizing a change in use of dedicated parkland, known as Country Club Creek West Greenbelt, to permanently use approximately 121,156 square feet of parkland in order to construct, operate, maintain, and repair roadway and associated improvements. Funding: This item includes a mitigation payment in the amount of $1,368,050 and $107,735 in the form of park improvements from Austin Transportation and Public Works to Austin Parks and Recreation and, as a result, there is no impact to the General Fund.

Authorize a contract for a policy and compliance management platform and related services to distribute and track department policies, document employee training, and support accreditation and audit readiness for all City departments with PowerDMS Inc. d/b/a Innovative Data Solutions Inc., for an initial term of one year in an estimated amount of $144,000 with up to four one-year extension options each in an estimated amount of $144,000 for a total contract amount not to exceed $720,000. Funding: $93,000 is available in the Operating Budget of various City departments. Funding for the remaining contract term is contingent upon available funding in future budgets.
